newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Jet fuel prices hit Pakistan's PIA.
newsitem.headline: Jet fuel prices hit Pakistan's PIA.

text.p: Soaring jet fuel costs could erode the profitability of Pakistan International Airline Corp (PIA), according to its managing director, Nawaz Tiwana.

The state-run airline now expects to spend 8.12 billion rupees ($202 million) on jet fuel in 1996/97 (July-June) compared to 5.82 billion in 1995/96, after prices jumped nearly 45 percent in July-December, Tiwana told Reuters on Monday.

"The total financial impact on PIA in the past six months is almost 1.05 billion rupees compared to the first half of fiscal 1995/96," he said. If the trend continued, PIA could face a jet fuel bill almost 2.3 billion rupees higher than last year's.
Tiwana said the extra cost could hammer the national carrier's expected profit of one billion rupees this year.

"This is a very unfortunate situation. Because of the additional fuel prices, the airline's profitability is going down, but we are taking measures to offset this by making more money elsewhere and cutting costs wherever possible," he said.

A PIA official said there were no immediate plans to raise fares, which last went up on December 16. Normal fares to all except Middle Eastern destinations increased 10 percent, while excursion fares and fares to the Middle East rose 15 percent.
PIA's after-tax profit plunged to 65 million rupees in 1995/96 from 293 million in the year-earlier period.
PIA paid no dividend or bonus stocks for the year ended June 30. Its 10-rupee share closed 0.25 rupee lower at 9.25 on Monday at the Karachi Stock Exchange.

Tiwana said prices of crude oil and products had risen dramatically in 1996, with jet fuel prices soaring because of higher demand and lower production due to the technical shut-down of some Far Eastern refineries.
He said prices had risen 48.44 percent in Karachi since July, 51.52 percent in Lahore, 50.64 percent in Islamabad, 47.90 percent in Peshawar and 51.33 percent in Quetta.
PIA imports most of the jet fuel for its 46-aircraft fleet.
